overview.headline: Comparing photosynthesis and chemosynthesis as energy for life

keyPoints.point: Students learn that photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into sugars and oxygen using solar energy.
keyPoints.quote: Photosynthesis: The process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into oxygen and sugars (food), using energy from the sun.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that chemosynthetic microbes create sugars using energy released from chemical reactions.
keyPoints.quote: Chemosynthesis: The process by which microbes create sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that matter cannot be created or destroyed during a chemical reaction.
keyPoints.quote: Remind students that the law of conservation of matter states that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that photosynthesis and chemosynthesis together fuel all life on Earth in different environments.
keyPoints.quote: Together, photosynthesis and chemosynthesis fuel all life on Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: Process that uses energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into sugars.
keyTerms.quote: Photosynthesis: The process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into oxygen and sugars (food), using energy from the sun.

keyTerms.gloss: Process where microbes create sugars using energy released from chemical reactions.
keyTerms.quote: Chemosynthesis: The process by which microbes create sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyTerms.gloss: Organisms that make their own food from raw materials and energy.
keyTerms.quote: Autotroph: Organisms that are able to make their own food from raw materials and energy, also known as producers.

keyTerms.gloss: Starting substance that changes during a chemical reaction.
keyTerms.quote: Reactants: A substance that changes in a chemical reaction.
